property_summary: After setting programOperators[nonOwner] to true, calling create() from nonOwner (who is not owner) with a non-zero roundImplementation and alloSettings, the reference contract sets roundImplementation to the clone address (because onlyOwner modifier prevents owner-only updates after create), but the buggy contract allows owner-only actions to be called by anyone, so roundImplementation remains unchanged after create() call. But the observable difference is that the reference contract's create() succeeds, while the buggy contract also succeeds, so the difference must be observed via state: after create(), the clone address is stored in roundImplementation in reference, but in buggy contract roundImplementation is unchanged because create() does not update roundImplementation. Actually the given difference says P.roundImplementation() != M.roundImplementation() after a create() call. Let me set up: deploy c, call updateRoundImplementation(someContract), call updateAlloSettings(someAddr), then set callerAsOperator via programOperators[caller] = true, then call create() from caller. In reference, onlyOwner modifier in updateRoundImplementation works correctly, allowing owner to set roundImplementation to a non-zero address; then create() succeeds and does not change roundImplementation. In buggy contract, onlyOwner modifier is bypassed, so anyone can call updateRoundImplementation. However the difference stated involves create() call. I will instead use a scenario where the bug causes create() to revert vs succeed based on ownership check: in reference, if msg.sender is not owner but is program operator, create() proceeds; in buggy, same behavior because onlyProgramOperator check is unaffected. Actually the bug disables onlyOwner, which is used in updateRoundImplementation and updateAlloSettings, not in create(). So the observable divergence must involve calling updateRoundImplementation after create? No, the statement: 'after a call to create() completes, the value of state variable roundImplementation differs: P.roundImplementation() != M.roundImplementation().' This means create() itself modifies roundImplementation in one version but not the other. Since create() does not modify roundImplementation in the contract code, the only way this happens is if create() calls clone which somehow changes roundImplementation? No, clone returns a new address, it doesn't assign to storage. The only state variable that create() modifies is none. Therefore the difference must arise from a different entry point or from a call within create() that triggers a modifier that updates state. Looking at the code, create() uses ClonesUpgradeable.clone(roundImplementation) which uses assembly create opcode — no state change. Then emits event and calls initialize on clone. So roundImplementation cannot change by create. The only external functions that modify roundImplementation are updateRoundImplementation() which uses onlyOwner. So the difference is: after someone calls updateRoundImplementation() (bypassing onlyOwner in bug), then create() succeeds in both but roundImplementation differs. For a concrete witness: deploy c, set programOperators[anyone]=true, set alloSettings=someAddress, then from a non-owner address that is a program operator, call c.create(encodedParameters, ownedBy). In reference, this succeeds and roundImplementation stays as previously set by owner (e.g., address(1)). In buggy, before create, the non-owner can call updateRoundImplementation to set roundImplementation to some other address (e.g., address(2)) because onlyOwner is bypassed. So after create, P.roundImplementation is address(1), M.roundImplementation is address(2). To observe: after calling updateRoundImplementation from non-owner, check roundImplementation value. So concrete test: set owner as address(this), set programOperators[nonOwner]=true, set alloSettings to some address, set roundImplementation to address(1) via owner call, then prank nonOwner call updateRoundImplementation(address(2)). In reference, this reverts because onlyOwner, so roundImplementation remains address(1). In buggy, it succeeds, so roundImplementation becomes address(2). Then assert that roundImplementation equals address(1) in reference and address(2) in bug. That distinction confirms the bug. So the test: deploy, from owner set programOperators[nonOwner]=true, set alloSettings=someAddress, set roundImplementation=address(1), then from nonOwner call updateRoundImplementation(address(2)). The reference call reverts (we can try/catch), the bug succeeds. Then assert: the call succeeded after prank(nonOwner) c.updateRoundImplementation? — but reference reverts. So we can assert that the revert boolean is true for reference, false for bug. But the test must pass on reference and fail on bug. Let the assertion be: try c.updateRoundImplementation(address(2)) { ok = true; } catch { ok = false; } Then assertTrue(ok == false) for reference (reverts) and assertTrue(ok == true) for bug. But wait: the test is written once, deployed against either version. We want it to PASS on reference (i.e., assertion holds) and FAIL on bug (assertion fails). So we set assertion such that it is true for reference and false for bug. For reference, the call reverts so ok == false; we want assertTrue(ok == false) which is true. For bug, ok == true, so assertTrue(ok == false) fails. Perfect. So implement with try/catch for updateRoundImplementation from nonOwner.
change_summary: Change the condition in onlyOwner modifier to always be true, disabling access control.
